title: The whole iceberg
caption: Write a skill the third time, describe it by the moment, and decide where the project details live before you share it.
analogy: The robot back on deck; the manual open at a short index.
takeaways: Each Section's takeaway at its depth

surface.name: Surface
surface.line1: A skill hands the AI your proven procedure on demand;
surface.line2: until a task needs it, the AI reads only its name and description.

sunlit.name: Sunlit
sunlit.line1: Write it from a run that worked;
sunlit.line2: the AI sees only its description.

twilight.name: Twilight
twilight.line1: A good skill does one job; to work in more than one project,
twilight.line2: it keeps project details beside it, in files it reads when it runs.

midnight.name: Midnight
midnight.line1: A shared skill is a knowledge article:
midnight.line2: it needs an owner, a version and a review date.

abyss.name: Abyss
abyss.line1: Keeping a skill right is the work: a model update changes who reads it,
abyss.line2: so test it again, and retire skills nobody uses.

index.title: Skill index
index.description: Takes a sediment core. Use when we reach a new site and need a sample from the seabed.

0.text: Pick one task you've explained three times, and turn a good run of it into a skill.
0.agent: Ask the agent to turn this conversation into a skill and save it to {path}.

1.text: Write its description as the moment you'd need it.
1.agent: The description: line in the front matter of SKILL.md.

2.text: Before sharing a skill, decide where the project details live, and give it an owner.
2.agent: Steps point to a project file such as CONTEXT.md; shared in this repository: .claude/skills/; shared across projects: a plugin, with an owner.

alt: The whole iceberg from the Surface to the Abyss: the ship at the waterline with the captain and the pilot on the bridge, the robot back on deck, and the manual open at a short index of three skills.

skill-governance-settled-and-not.header: Skill governance: what is settled, and what is not
skill-governance-settled-and-not.description: no source defines owner and review date as a rule for skills, and none shows how many organisations govern shared skills at all [1]. The audience-by-scope matrix is a rule of thumb, not a published framework [2].

skilldex.title: Saha and Hemanth, Skilldex: A Package Manager and Registry for Agent Skill Packages with Hierarchical Scope-Based Distribution

three-steps.title: Three steps
three-steps.script: Let me bring the three steps up from the seabed. One: pick a task you have explained three times, and turn a good run of it into a skill. Two: write its description as the moment you would need it. Three: before you share it, decide where the project details live, and give it an owner.

the-honest-caveat.title: The honest caveat
the-honest-caveat.script: I want to be honest about the deep end. Governance, review and retirement are the part I am least sure about, and I am still learning there too. If you find something that works, tell me.

your-first-card.title: Your first card
your-first-card.script: We are back on deck, with a short index. If you want a low-key start, take the task you explained last week and turn its best run into your first skill. Thank you.
